paragraphs.en: I am by birth a Genevese, and my family is one of the most distinguished of that republic. My ancestors had been for many years counsellors and syndics, and my father had filled several public situations with honour and reputation. He was respected by all who knew him for his integrity and indefatigable attention to public business. He passed his younger days perpetually occupied by the affairs of his country; a variety of circumstances had prevented his marrying early, nor was it until the decline of life that he became a husband and the father of a family.
paragraphs.zh: 我出生在日内瓦，我们家族是这个共和国中最显赫的家族之一。我的祖先多年来一直担任顾问和市议员，我的父亲也以荣誉和声望担任过多个公职。凡是认识他的人，都因他的正直和勤勉而尊敬他。他年轻时一直忙于国家事务；由于各种原因，他未能及早结婚，直到晚年才成家并成为父亲。

paragraphs.en: As the circumstances of his marriage illustrate his character, I cannot refrain from relating them. One of his most intimate friends was a merchant who, from a flourishing state, fell, through numerous mischances, into poverty. This man, whose name was Beaufort, was of a proud and unbending disposition and could not bear to live in poverty and oblivion in the same country where he had formerly been distinguished for his rank and magnificence. Having paid his debts, therefore, in the most honourable manner, he retreated with his daughter to the town of Lucerne, where he lived unknown and in wretchedness. My father loved Beaufort with the truest friendship and was deeply grieved by his retreat in these unfortunate circumstances. He bitterly deplored the false pride which led his friend to a conduct so little worthy of the affection that united them. He lost no time in endeavouring to seek him out, with the hope of persuading him to begin the world again through his credit and assistance.
paragraphs.zh: 正如他的婚姻状况体现了他的性格，我无法不将它讲述出来。他最亲密的朋友之一是个商人，原本家道殷实，但因屡遭不幸，最终沦入贫困。这位名叫博福特的人性格高傲倔强，无法忍受在曾经以地位和奢华著称的国家里过着贫穷而被人遗忘的生活。因此，他以最光荣的方式还清了所有债务，带着女儿退隐到卢塞恩城，在那里他默默无闻，过着隐居的生活。 苦难。我父亲对鲍福特怀有最真挚的友谊，对于他在这种不幸的情况下退隐感到非常悲痛。他痛心地谴责那种虚伪的自尊心，正是这种自尊心导致他的朋友做出如此不配他们之间深厚情谊的行为。他立刻开始努力寻找鲍福特，希望能说服他借助他的信誉和帮助重新开始自己的事业。

paragraphs.en: Beaufort had taken effectual measures to conceal himself, and it was ten months before my father discovered his abode. Overjoyed at this discovery, he hastened to the house, which was situated in a mean street near the Reuss. But when he entered, misery and despair alone welcomed him. Beaufort had saved but a very small sum of money from the wreck of his fortunes, but it was sufficient to provide him with sustenance for some months, and in the meantime he hoped to procure some respectable employment in a merchant’s house. The interval was, consequently, spent in inaction; his grief only became more deep and rankling when he had leisure for reflection, and at length it took so fast hold of his mind that at the end of three months he lay on a bed of sickness, incapable of any exertion.
paragraphs.zh: 博福特采取了有效的措施来隐藏自己，直到十个月后我父亲才发现了他的住所。得知这一发现后，父亲欣喜若狂，立刻前往那所房子，它位于罗伊斯河附近的一条贫民街。但当他走进去时，迎接他的只有痛苦和绝望。博福特从破产中仅剩下一小笔钱，但这足以让他维持几个月的生活，同时他希望在这期间能在某家商行找到一份体面的工作。因此，这段时间他只能无所事事地度过，他的悲伤也因此愈发加深。 当他有空闲时间进行反思时，这种感觉更加深刻而令人痛苦，最终这种情绪深深困扰着他的心灵，三个月后，他病倒在床上，无法进行任何活动。

paragraphs.en: His daughter attended him with the greatest tenderness, but she saw with despair that their little fund was rapidly decreasing and that there was no other prospect of support. But Caroline Beaufort possessed a mind of an uncommon mould, and her courage rose to support her in her adversity. She procured plain work; she plaited straw and by various means contrived to earn a pittance scarcely sufficient to support life.
paragraphs.zh: 他的女儿以极大的温柔照顾着他，但她绝望地看到，他们微薄的积蓄正在迅速减少，而再没有其他经济来源。但卡罗琳·鲍福特拥有一颗不同寻常的坚强心灵，她的勇气在逆境中愈发坚定。她找来一些简单的手工活，编结草帽，又通过各种方式设法赚取微薄的收入，仅仅够维持生活。

paragraphs.en: Several months passed in this manner. Her father grew worse; her time was more entirely occupied in attending him; her means of subsistence decreased; and in the tenth month her father died in her arms, leaving her an orphan and a beggar. This last blow overcame her, and she knelt by Beaufort’s coffin weeping bitterly, when my father entered the chamber. He came like a protecting spirit to the poor girl, who committed herself to his care; and after the interment of his friend he conducted her to Geneva and placed her under the protection of a relation. Two years after this event Caroline became his wife.
paragraphs.zh: 这样又过了几个月。她的父亲病情日益加重，她的时间完全被照顾父亲占据，她的生活来源也逐渐减少。到了第十个月，父亲死在她的怀抱中，使她成了一个孤儿和乞丐。这一打击使她难以承受，她跪在博福特的棺材旁痛哭流涕，这时我的父亲走进了房间。他像一个保护者一样来到这个无助的女孩身边，她将自己托付给他照顾。在安葬了好友之后，他带她去了日内瓦，并将她托付给一位亲戚照顾。两年后，卡罗琳 成了他的妻子。

paragraphs.en: There was a considerable difference between the ages of my parents, but this circumstance seemed to unite them only closer in bonds of devoted affection. There was a sense of justice in my father’s upright mind which rendered it necessary that he should approve highly to love strongly. Perhaps during former years he had suffered from the late-discovered unworthiness of one beloved and so was disposed to set a greater value on tried worth. There was a show of gratitude and worship in his attachment to my mother, differing wholly from the doting fondness of age, for it was inspired by reverence for her virtues and a desire to be the means of, in some degree, recompensing her for the sorrows she had endured, but which gave inexpressible grace to his behaviour to her. Everything was made to yield to her wishes and her convenience. He strove to shelter her, as a fair exotic is sheltered by the gardener, from every rougher wind and to surround her with all that could tend to excite pleasurable emotion in her soft and benevolent mind. Her health, and even the tranquillity of her hitherto constant spirit, had been shaken by what she had gone through. During the two years that had elapsed previous to their marriage my father had gradually relinquished all his public functions; and immediately after their union they sought the pleasant climate of Italy, and the change of scene and interest attendant on a tour through that land of wonders, as a restorative for her weakened frame.
paragraphs.zh: 我的父母年龄相差较大，但这种情形似乎反而使他们更加紧密地结合在忠贞的爱恋之中。我父亲正直的内心中有一种正义感，这使得他若要喜爱，就必定会深爱。也许在以前的岁月里，他曾因发现所爱之人后来显露出不值得爱的品格而受过苦，因此更珍惜经过考验的美德。他对母亲的依恋中流露出感激与崇敬之情，这与老年人的溺爱完全不同，因为这种依恋源于敬重。 为了她的美德，也为了想在某种程度上补偿她所经受的痛苦，这使他在对待她时表现出难以言喻的优雅。一切都要让位于她的意愿和方便。他努力保护她，就像园丁保护美丽的异国花卉一样，使她免受狂风的侵袭，并围绕她安排一切能唤起她温柔仁慈心灵中愉悦情绪的事物。她原本一直平静的心灵，以及她的健康，都因她所经历的一切而受到了动摇。在过去的两年里， 在他们结婚之前，我父亲已逐渐辞去了所有公众职务；结婚后，他们立即前往意大利，寻求那里的宜人气候，以及游览这个奇迹之国所带来的环境和兴趣的改变，以此来调养她虚弱的身体。

paragraphs.en: From Italy they visited Germany and France. I, their eldest child, was born at Naples, and as an infant accompanied them in their rambles. I remained for several years their only child. Much as they were attached to each other, they seemed to draw inexhaustible stores of affection from a very mine of love to bestow them upon me. My mother’s tender caresses and my father’s smile of benevolent pleasure while regarding me are my first recollections. I was their plaything and their idol, and something better—their child, the innocent and helpless creature bestowed on them by Heaven, whom to bring up to good, and whose future lot it was in their hands to direct to happiness or misery, according as they fulfilled their duties towards me. With this deep consciousness of what they owed towards the being to which they had given life, added to the active spirit of tenderness that animated both, it may be imagined that while during every hour of my infant life I received a lesson of patience, of charity, and of self-control, I was so guided by a silken cord that all seemed but one train of enjoyment to me.
paragraphs.zh: 他们从意大利去了德国和法国。我作为他们最大的孩子，出生于那不勒斯，婴儿时期就跟着他们四处游历。好几年里，我都是他们唯一的孩子。尽管他们彼此非常恩爱，但似乎从一个充满爱的源泉中汲取了无穷无尽的温情，全部倾注在我身上。母亲温柔的爱抚和父亲看着我时脸上流露出的慈祥愉悦的笑容，是我最初的记忆。我是他们的玩伴，他们的偶像，更是比这些更珍贵的东西——他们的孩子，一个天赐的天真无助的生物，他们要将我抚养成人。 他们对我负有责任，我未来的命运也掌握在他们手中，是幸福还是痛苦，全看他们是否尽到了对我的责任。怀着这种对生命给予者所应尽的深切责任感，再加上他们内心充满的温柔情感，可以想象，在我婴儿时期每一刻，我都受到了耐心、仁爱和自我克制的教育。我仿佛被一条丝带牵引着，一切似乎都成了我的快乐经历。

paragraphs.en: For a long time I was their only care. My mother had much desired to have a daughter, but I continued their single offspring. When I was about five years old, while making an excursion beyond the frontiers of Italy, they passed a week on the shores of the Lake of Como. Their benevolent disposition often made them enter the cottages of the poor. This, to my mother, was more than a duty; it was a necessity, a passion—remembering what she had suffered, and how she had been relieved—for her to act in her turn the guardian angel to the afflicted. During one of their walks a poor cot in the foldings of a vale attracted their notice as being singularly disconsolate, while the number of half-clothed children gathered about it spoke of penury in its worst shape. One day, when my father had gone by himself to Milan, my mother, accompanied by me, visited this abode. She found a peasant and his wife, hard working, bent down by care and labour, distributing a scanty meal to five hungry babes. Among these there was one which attracted my mother far above all the rest. She appeared of a different stock. The four others were dark-eyed, hardy little vagrants; this child was thin and very fair. Her hair was the brightest living gold, and despite the poverty of her clothing, seemed to set a crown of distinction on her head. Her brow was clear and ample, her blue eyes cloudless, and her lips and the moulding of her face so expressive of sensibility and sweetness that none could behold her without looking on her as of a distinct species, a being heaven-sent, and bearing a celestial stamp in all her features.
paragraphs.zh: 很长一段时间里，我一直是他们唯一的牵挂。我母亲非常希望有个女儿，但我却一直是他们唯一的子女。当我大约五岁时，他们带我出了一次远门，越过了意大利的边界，在科莫湖的湖岸度过了一个星期。他们仁慈的性格常常使他们走进穷人的小屋。这对我的母亲来说，与其说是一种责任，不如说是一种需要，一种激情——她记得自己曾经受过的苦，以及她是如何得到帮助的，因此她也想转而成为那些受难者的守护天使。在一次散步途中，他们进入了一个贫穷农家的茅舍。 一个山谷引起了他们的注意，因为它显得格外凄凉，而围绕在它周围的半裸孩子数量之多，说明了贫穷到了最恶劣的程度。有一天，我父亲独自去了米兰，我母亲带着我前去探访这个住所。她发现一个农民和他的妻子，他们勤劳而辛劳，正将少量的食物分给五个饥饿的孩子。在这些孩子中，有一个特别引起了我母亲的注意，远远超过其他孩子。这个孩子似乎出自不同的家世。其他四个孩子都是黑眼睛、身体健壮的小流浪儿，而这个孩子却瘦弱且非常白皙。 她的头发是鲜活的金色，尽管衣着贫寒，却仿佛在她头上戴了一顶与众不同的王冠。她的前额开阔而明朗，蓝眼睛清澈无瑕，她的嘴唇以及脸部的轮廓充满敏感与温婉，使人一见便觉得她属于另一个种类，是天赐的生灵，她的所有容貌都带着神圣的印记。

paragraphs.en: The peasant woman, perceiving that my mother fixed eyes of wonder and admiration on this lovely girl, eagerly communicated her history. She was not her child, but the daughter of a Milanese nobleman. Her mother was a German and had died on giving her birth. The infant had been placed with these good people to nurse: they were better off then. They had not been long married, and their eldest child was but just born. The father of their charge was one of those Italians nursed in the memory of the antique glory of Italy—one among the _schiavi ognor frementi,_ who exerted himself to obtain the liberty of his country. He became the victim of its weakness. Whether he had died or still lingered in the dungeons of Austria was not known. His property was confiscated; his child became an orphan and a beggar. She continued with her foster parents and bloomed in their rude abode, fairer than a garden rose among dark-leaved brambles.
paragraphs.zh: 农妇见我母亲对这个漂亮女孩投以惊奇和钦佩的目光，便急切地向我们讲述了她的身世。她并不是自己的孩子，而是米兰一位贵族的女儿。她的母亲是德国人，在生她时去世了。这个婴儿被送到这对善良的人家哺乳；那时他们还比较富裕。他们结婚不久，最大的孩子刚刚出生。这个孩子的父亲是那些铭记意大利古代光荣的意大利人之一——属于那些“永远躁动的奴隶”中的一员，他竭尽全力去争取…… 他祖国的自由。他成了其软弱的牺牲品。他究竟是死了，还是仍在奥地利的地牢中苟延残喘，无人知晓。他的财产被没收；他的孩子成了孤儿，沦为乞丐。她继续和养父母生活在一起，在他们粗陋的住所中成长，比荆棘丛中的花园玫瑰还要娇艳。

paragraphs.en: When my father returned from Milan, he found playing with me in the hall of our villa a child fairer than pictured cherub—a creature who seemed to shed radiance from her looks and whose form and motions were lighter than the chamois of the hills. The apparition was soon explained. With his permission my mother prevailed on her rustic guardians to yield their charge to her. They were fond of the sweet orphan. Her presence had seemed a blessing to them, but it would be unfair to her to keep her in poverty and want when Providence afforded her such powerful protection. They consulted their village priest, and the result was that Elizabeth Lavenza became the inmate of my parents’ house—my more than sister—the beautiful and adored companion of all my occupations and my pleasures.
paragraphs.zh: 当我父亲从米兰回来时，他在我们别墅的走廊里发现有一个孩子正和我玩耍，那孩子比画中的天使还要美丽——她似乎从容貌中散发出光芒，她的身形和动作比山间的岩羚羊还要轻盈。这个幻影很快得到了解释。在得到他允许的情况下，母亲说服了她乡下的监护人，让他们把这孩子交给她。他们很喜欢这个可爱的孤儿。她在那里似乎给她们带来了祝福，但若在她拥有如此强大保护者的情况下，仍让她留在贫困中，那是不公平的。他们商议了之后， 村里的神父，结果就是伊丽莎白·拉文扎成了我父母家中的一名寄宿者——比我亲妹妹还要亲密——她是我所有活动和欢乐中的美丽而受宠爱的伴侣。

paragraphs.en: Everyone loved Elizabeth. The passionate and almost reverential attachment with which all regarded her became, while I shared it, my pride and my delight. On the evening previous to her being brought to my home, my mother had said playfully, “I have a pretty present for my Victor—tomorrow he shall have it.” And when, on the morrow, she presented Elizabeth to me as her promised gift, I, with childish seriousness, interpreted her words literally and looked upon Elizabeth as mine—mine to protect, love, and cherish. All praises bestowed on her I received as made to a possession of my own. We called each other familiarly by the name of cousin. No word, no expression could body forth the kind of relation in which she stood to me—my more than sister, since till death she was to be mine only.
paragraphs.zh: 每个人都爱伊丽莎白。所有人对她的热情而近乎崇拜的依恋之情，虽然我与他们一样，但这也成了我的骄傲与快乐。在她来到我家的前一晚，我母亲开玩笑地说：“我给我的维克多准备了一份漂亮的礼物——明天他就能得到。”第二天，当她把伊丽莎白介绍给我，说这是她答应送给我的礼物时，我以孩子般认真的态度，把她说的话当了真，把伊丽莎白看作是我的——我应该保护、爱惜和珍视的人。所有对她的赞美，我都当作是对我自己所有之物的赞美。我们 他们彼此亲热地称呼对方为表亲。没有任何言语或表达方式能够传达她与我之间的关系——她比我姐妹更亲密，因为直到死亡，她都只能属于我一个人。
